name: Quartz Grey
lede: Quartz grey is a warm, dark grey with a trace of olive, named in the RAL system for the common mineral.

sections.title: A mineral and a code
sections.body:
Our library carries the name from RAL, the German color-standard system, as RAL 7039 with a first record of 1927, and gives its swatch only as an approximate screen value [1]. The name borrows quartz, the silica mineral [2].

The *Pigment Compendium* notes that quartz is found close to colorless or white, and impurities give the colored varieties: rose quartz is pink, citrine yellow, amethyst purple, and smoky quartz a grey-brown that may contain aluminium [2]. The books do not say that RAL named its grey after smoky quartz, so treat the link as a likely hint, not a fact [1][2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This is a very common painted color: our archive of 23,781 paintings has it in 1,596 (6.71%), as photographed [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a mid-tone, and Ruisdael, with it in 7 of 18 works, is its most devoted painter [3]. The earliest match is from the 1100s, 800 years before the name existed, so these are look-alike greys in aged paint, not proof of any pigment [3]. Neighbors are [[slate-grey]], [[taupe]] and [[grey]] [1].

questions.q: Which system gives Quartz Grey its code, RAL 7039?
What color is smoky quartz, per the Pigment Compendium?

openers: Smoky quartz is a grey-brown, but the books do not say RAL named Quartz Grey after it.

issues: Claims verified against fact card and book text; no changes.
